newsitem.title: INDIA: Bombay stocks end mixed in lacklustre trade.
newsitem.headline: Bombay stocks end mixed in lacklustre trade.

text.p: Share prices finished mixed at the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) on Thursday in the absence of any major market moving news, traders said.
Brokers said some short-covering and scattered buying by local funds helped select stocks end marginally higher.
The 30-share BSE Index gained 8.50 points or 0.25 percent at a provisional close of 3,391.21, the day's high after falling to 3,348.75 in mid-session.
The 50-stock National Stock Exchange Index was up 0.45 points or 0.05 percent at a provisional 991.45 close.
"Short-covering by operators at close pushed up the market, but there was not much action in pivotals," said Dilip Joshi, dealer at Prime Broking.

On Wednesday, Finance Minister P. Chidambaram stuck to a minimum alternate tax (MAT), widely opposed by industry while offering to exempt ailing firms and companies located in backward areas from the tax.
"We do not expect these marginal sops to alter the sentiment and the market is likely to remain weak," Jardine Fleming's market strategist Ritu Gupte said.
The 12.9 percent tax proposed by the government last July is targetted at firms which currently paid no taxes by ploughing back profits into tax-spared dividends and diversifications.
The 500-share CRISIL index lost 0.35 points to a provisional close of 669.52.
In late trade, pivotals staged a smart rally to end higher. SBI was up 4.25 rupees at 273 rupees, Reliance 1.0 at 203.25, Gujarat Ambuja Cement 6.50 at 294 and Bajaj Auto 1.0 at 987.25.
Pivotal stocks which fell included TELCO down 5.50 rupees to 459.75, Grasim 5.25 to 431.75, Indian Hotels 8.50 to 751.50 and Mahindra & Mahindra 2.0 to 351.25.
